beats.text: You can download a 30 billion parameter brain from Meta tonight. Nobody at Meta led with that.
beats.show_cue: The Muse Glimmer model page full frame, held on the model name, the Meta Superintelligence Lab org, and the apache-2.0 licence tag.

beats.text: Meta spent the day on a 6,000 word essay that says superintelligent about 60 times, while the thing you can touch, Muse Glimmer, slipped onto Hugging Face with an Apache licence and a build that fits one gaming card. The essay got the headlines.
beats.show_cue: Meta's essay page scrolling fast so superintelligent keeps flying past, then cut to the model page tab. The essay page is heavy, open it in a browser and let it settle before recording.

beats.text: The download is the story. Open weights means the brain itself is a file on your drive. No bill per question, nothing leaves the room, and Meta claims decoding runs 3.1 times faster.
beats.show_cue: The model page's Files tab, the model literally a list of files, then the Target Hardware table with the 24GB VRAM column readable.

beats.text: The file is not the recipe, the 24 gig figure is the squeezed version, full precision wants 64, and the bigger Muse Spark still hasn't shipped.
beats.show_cue: The hardware table held on the quantized 24GB row beside the 64GB full precision row, then the coverage paragraph reporting Muse Spark 1.2 is still weeks away.

beats.text: If you shelved a local agent project over cost, price it again. The card is on you.
beats.show_cue: Operator on camera, the model page in a small corner inset.

beats.text: Follow Straw Motion. We skip the hype, you get the story.
beats.show_cue: Straw Motion logo end card, no overlay.
